summary: The remit rail is an optional module inside the single core process (attest/apps/core/src/remit, REMIT_ENABLED). It drives a VN to SG settlement state machine: REQUEST_ACCEPTED, BANK_AUTHORIZED, TRAVEL_RULE_PENDING, PAYOUT_PRE_APPROVED, ONCHAIN_SETTLED, PAYOUT_IN_PROGRESS, BENEFICIARY_CREDIT_CONFIRMED and EVIDENCE_ANCHORED, plus the terminal states CANCELLED, RETURNED and EXCEPTION. Its counterparty is a partner simulator (demo-partners :3300) that plays the BFI, the payout bank and the settlement wallet on a local anvil chain. The first two states are set inside the POST /v1/settlements request. The next three legs run in-process as a fire-and-forget setImmediate chain that makes four sequential partner HTTP calls (20 s timeout, no retry). Signed BFI callbacks drive the payout states, and reconciliation, evidence packaging and one attestation leaf per payment all run inside the PAYOUT_COMPLETED callback request. The RemitWorker only promotes EVIDENCE_ANCHORED and delivers webhooks, on a hardcoded 2 s tick. One happy-path payment costs about 165 SQL statements (about 109 reads and 56 autocommit writes), 22 platform ES256 signatures, about 16 verifications, 1 JWE, 4 outbound partner calls, 3 inbound callbacks and 11 signed webhooks. Payments share Merkle batches (up to 1,024 leaves per Bitcoin anchor), so anchoring cost is spread across them. The first hard ceiling is the webhook outbox: 20 deliveries per 2 s tick, one at a time, 5 s timeout. That is 10 per second, or about 0.9 payments per second for orgs with a webhook URL, which is below T1. The pipeline has no durable queue, no backpressure, no recovery sweep and no retry. A restart strands in-flight payments, and any partner timeout leaves a payment in terminal EXCEPTION. State changes are read-then-write with no compare-and-set, and event sequence numbers are MAX(seq)+1. Concurrent cancel, RFI-answer and callback paths can therefore lose updates or issue a second settlement instruction, and the UNIQUE (payment_id, seq) key is the only guard, a probabilistic one. promoteAnchored full-scans remit_payments every 2 s with no LIMIT. Bank-side SDK polling (every 1.5 to 3 s, each poll audited) and the SDK's LIKE-based duplicate search add load comparable to the pipeline itself. The settlement leg is sandbox-only: anvil unlocked account, automine, 1-confirmation finality, five reused deposit addresses, one transfer per payment, synchronous wait. The simulator rewrites whole JSON files on every update, so it would not sustain T1 for long (estimate). T1 is reachable after targeted fixes. T2 needs a durable job queue, far fewer statements per payment, multi-instance safety and an asynchronous settlement leg on a real chain. T3 needs net settlement (one transfer per batch, not per payment), sharding and batched signing.

components.name: Remit API routes
components.role: HTTP surface: POST /v1/quotes; POST /v1/settlements (Idempotency-Key required); GET ledger, detail, evidence and on-chain status; cancel; rfi-response; daily manifests; anonymous BFI callbacks; console product activation; sandbox registry admin
components.tech: node:http router, TypeScript run by Node 22 type stripping
components.notes: No rate limiter on any remit route. 1 MiB JSON body cap. Every API-key call except a few console GETs writes an audit_log row, awaited before the response. Callbacks are anonymous and not audited.

components.name: RemitOrchestrator
components.role: State machine driver: synchronous acceptance (REQUEST_ACCEPTED, then BANK_AUTHORIZED), in-process async pipeline via setImmediate (travel rule, payout approval, USDC transfer), BFI callback handling, six-axis reconciliation, evidence commit, anchored promotion
components.notes: advance() can resume from any state, but nothing calls it after a restart. Callers are acceptSettlement and respondRfi only.

components.name: RemitStore
components.role: Payments, append-only signed events, quotes, idempotency keys, travel-rule ciphertexts; forward-only transition(); keyset ledger search
components.tech: MySQL 8 via mysql2 pool (SQLite in tests)
components.notes: No transactions. transition() reads, checks, then UPDATEs by id only. Event seq = MAX(seq)+1, backed by UNIQUE (payment_id, seq). store.get is SELECT *.

components.name: RemitWorker
components.role: Timer in the core process: promoteAnchored(), then outbox.deliverDue(); process-local running flag
components.notes: Tick hardcoded to 2,000 ms whenever WORKER_TICK_MS > 0. Does not advance payments through the pipeline.

components.name: WebhookOutbox
components.role: Table-backed, platform-signed, at-least-once bank notifications with a backoff ladder; bank polling is the backstop
components.notes: 20 rows per tick, sequential, 5 s timeout, 5 attempts, never pruned

components.name: Trust Registry and subscriptions
components.role: Institution keys and roles, product subscriptions (webhook URL lives in config JSON), verification keyring, registry snapshot
components.notes: Uncached. list() is a full-table read used several times per payment.

components.name: Signing and encryption
components.role: ES256 event and element signatures; platform key PEM created at first boot; ECDH-ES + A256GCM JWE for the Travel Rule payload
components.notes: verifyEvent re-parses the SPKI on every call. The platform key is a file on local disk (sandbox custody).

components.name: Evidence and reconciliation
components.role: Collect the signed elements from events, verify them against the registry keyring, evaluate six axes, assemble the package (all events, policy, verdict, full registry snapshot), compute the nonce'd commitment, then svc.issue (one attestation leaf per payment)
components.tech: attest-rules engine, WebCrypto verify (cached imported keys)

components.name: Quote engine and IVMS101 mapper
components.role: Static-rate VN to SG quotes (BigInt fixed point, TTL 600 s); mode A Travel Rule message shaping and required-field check

components.name: Partner connector
components.role: BfiConnector and SettlementWallet interfaces; TripleAProfileSim HTTP client used as both

components.name: Chain status lookup
components.role: On-demand read of a settlement transaction for GET /v1/settlements/:id/chain
components.notes: Not in the payment path. 5 s timeout per call, no cache.

components.name: Partner simulator (demo-partners)
components.role: Sandbox BFI (decrypt Travel Rule, screen, pre-approve, watch chain, FX, callbacks), SG payout bank (FAST sim ledger), settlement wallet (ERC-20 transfer from treasury)
components.tech: Node .mjs, anvil JSON-RPC with unlocked accounts, JSON files as books
components.notes: Sandbox-only. One process, three signing keys.

components.name: Settlement chain (anvil)
components.role: Local EVM chain eip155:31337 with MockUSDC; automine (one block per transaction); in-memory
components.notes: Sandbox-only. No nonce management in code; anvil assigns nonces for the unlocked treasury.

components.name: Bank SDK and SWIFT adapter
components.role: Runs at the bank: builds and signs instructions (in-process key or external HSM signer), submits, polls status, follows a folder of MT103, pacs.008 and pain.001 files, writes pacs.002 reports
components.notes: Not part of core. Its polling and duplicate searches are server load. Core never parses SWIFT.

flows.name: Quote and settlement acceptance
steps: Bank SDK POST /v1/quotes: requireAuth (api_keys SELECT + SHA-256), requireRemit (subscription + institution SELECT), buildQuote (static rates, TTL 600 s), INSERT remit_quotes, audit INSERT (routes.ts:380-388)
Bank signs 3 evidence elements + bank_authorization (+ fields_assertion in mode B), locally or via HSM (client.ts:557-567)

POST /v1/settlements: Idempotency-Key of at least 8 chars; idempotencyHit SELECT; same body hash replays the cached 202, a different body gets 409 (routes.ts:395-412); payment_id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,63}$ (routes.ts:49)

acceptSettlement: global payment_id existence check (409), quote exists, belongs to the org, not expired, amounts restate it exactly; BFI registered with an encryption key; verify bank_signature; travel-rule completeness (mode A) or bank-signed fields_assertion (mode B); verify the 3 elements (orchestrator.ts:147-249)
INSERT payment (REQUEST_ACCEPTED); events REQUEST_ACCEPTED, BANK_EVIDENCE_SUBMITTED, BANK_AUTHORIZATION_VERIFIED; transition BANK_AUTHORIZED; enqueue webhook (orchestrator.ts:252-284)
setImmediate(advance) scheduled; REPLACE INTO remit_idempotency; audit_log INSERT awaited; 202 returned (orchestrator.ts:287-293, routes.ts:420-422, http/routes.ts:130-133)

flows.name: Async pipeline: travel rule, payout approval, USDC transfer
flows.sync_or_async: async, in-process setImmediate chain (not a queue, not the worker)
steps: advance() reads the state and runs whichever legs remain (orchestrator.ts:304-322)

travelRuleLeg: mode A builds IVMS101 and JWE-encrypts it to the BFI; saves ciphertext + digest; scrubs plaintext; event TRAVEL_RULE_SENT; state TRAVEL_RULE_PENDING; webhook; POST /bfi/travel-rule (20 s). ACK is verified and appended as TRAVEL_RULE_RECEIVED. RFI pauses (bank answers via rfi-response). REJECTED leads to CANCELLED (orchestrator.ts:341-423)

approvalLeg: POST /bfi/payout-approval; verify BFI signature; event PAYOUT_ACCEPTED; patch deposit_address; state PAYOUT_PRE_APPROVED; webhook (orchestrator.ts:520-552). Sim: deposit address from a pool of 5, valid_until 15 min (server.mjs:240-242)

transferLeg: sign the instruction; event SETTLEMENT_INSTRUCTED; webhook; POST /wallet/transfer. The sim checks policy, sends eth_sendTransaction from the unlocked treasury and polls the receipt (at most 50 x 200 ms) before answering. Then verify the wallet signature; event USDC_TRANSFER_CONFIRMED; patch chain_tx; state ONCHAIN_SETTLED; webhook; POST /bfi/settlement-notice (orchestrator.ts:554-593; server.mjs:280-327; client.mjs:101-113)
Any throw: event EXCEPTION, terminal state, webhook. No retry and no resume (orchestrator.ts:323-338)

flows.name: BFI callbacks, payout, reconciliation, evidence commit
flows.sync_or_async: Simulator side async (watch loop); each callback is processed synchronously inside its HTTP request
steps: Sim watchAndPayout polls eth_getLogs once a second, for up to 60 s, until the deposit is seen (server.mjs:375-386)
POST /v1/remit/callbacks USDC_RECEIVED: verify BFI signature; event; state PAYOUT_IN_PROGRESS; webhook. No state precondition (orchestrator.ts:609-613)
PAYOUT_SUBMITTED: event + webhook (orchestrator.ts:615-618)

PAYOUT_COMPLETED: L1 appends EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT and holds. L2/L3 run reconcilePayment (all events, registry keyring, 6 WebCrypto verifies, evaluate), then SETTLEMENT_RECONCILED, then BENEFICIARY_CREDIT_CONFIRMED (or EXCEPTION), webhook, assemblePackage (all events + full registry), commitment, svc.issue (one attestation leaf), EVIDENCE_COMMITTED + webhook. All inside the callback request (orchestrator.ts:620-650, 677-736)
PAYOUT_FAILED then USDC_RETURNED leads to RETURNED (orchestrator.ts:651-669)
The sim gives each callback 10 s and never retries; a failure leaves its own ledger at ERROR (server.mjs:330-356)

flows.name: Evidence anchoring promotion
flows.sync_or_async: async (RemitWorker 2 s tick, plus the attest BatchWorker)
steps: The attest BatchWorker batches the evidence leaf (BATCH_MAX_LEAVES 1024, flush 15 s, WORKER_TICK_MS 3000 live) and anchors it on regtest, generating one block after each anchor (main.ts:131-143)
RemitWorker tick: anchoredPending joins remit_payments to attestations where status is 'confirmed', no LIMIT (store.ts:307-313)
For each row, sequentially: store.get, event EVIDENCE_ANCHORED, transition, webhook (orchestrator.ts:743-757)

flows.name: Webhook delivery
steps: enqueue: skipped if the org has no webhook_url; otherwise sign the envelope and INSERT (webhook.ts:51-73)
deliverDue: SELECT pending and due ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 20 (webhook.ts:77-80)
for-await POST each, 5 s timeout; 2xx marks it delivered; otherwise reschedule after 2 s, 10 s, 30 s, 120 s; marked exhausted at attempt 5, after which the bank must poll (webhook.ts:83-118)

flows.name: RFI answer and cancel
flows.sync_or_async: sync HTTP; RFI then resumes the async pipeline
steps: rfi-response: requires TRAVEL_RULE_PENDING with an RFI event and no TRAVEL_RULE_RECEIVED (no lock); verify bank signature; platform JWE-encrypts the answers; POST /bfi/travel-rule-response; events; setImmediate(advance) (orchestrator.ts:429-481)
cancel: allowed in REQUEST_ACCEPTED, BANK_AUTHORIZED or TRAVEL_RULE_PENDING; verify bank signature; event; CANCELLED; webhook; best-effort POST /bfi/cancel (orchestrator.ts:489-518)

flows.name: SWIFT folder adapter (bank side)
flows.sync_or_async: async polling loop at the bank
steps: Poll the inbox every 3 s; a file is taken once unchanged for 2 s; files over 4 MiB are refused; parseSwiftMessages returns every transaction in the file (adapter.ts:236-290)

For each transaction, sequentially: submitSwift runs knownSwift (GET by id, plus up to 2 pages of ?q= search per reference, plus GETs per hit), POST /v1/quotes, 4-5 signatures (an external signer spawns one process per signature), POST /v1/settlements (adapter.ts:292-296; client.ts:844-856)

Follow every open payment with GET /v1/settlements/:id on each pass (parked ones every 60 s, EXCEPTION ones for 24 h); write pacs.002 XML and status JSON on change; fetch and re-verify evidence at EVIDENCE_ANCHORED (adapter.ts:410-481)

flows.name: Daily manifest
steps: Bank signs {date, institution_id, payment_ids[], count} (client.ts:959-961)
Server verifies, selects all of the org's payments with substr(created_at,1,10)=date, diffs both ways, signs the verdict, issues an attestation, upserts remit_manifests (routes.ts:563-640)

capacity_findings.title: Pipeline runs as in-process fire-and-forget chains: no durable queue, no backpressure, no recovery
capacity_findings.affects: every payment between acceptance and ONCHAIN_SETTLED
capacity_findings.claim: After acceptance, each payment's next three legs run in a setImmediate chain inside the core process. Nothing persists the work item, nothing bounds concurrency, and nothing re-drives non-terminal payments: the RemitWorker only promotes anchored payments and delivers webhooks. A restart, deploy or crash leaves every payment that is mid-pipeline (BANK_AUTHORIZED, TRAVEL_RULE_PENDING after ACK, PAYOUT_PRE_APPROVED) stuck permanently. An unanswered RFI never times out to CANCELLED, although the design says it should. A burst starts one chain per accepted payment, and all of them contend for 10 DB connections and the partner.

attest/apps/core/src/remit/worker.ts:41-43 — const promoted = await this.orchestrator.promoteAnchored(); ... await this.outbox.deliverDue();
attest/apps/core/src/main.ts:151-153 — server.close(() => { void db.close().finally(() => process.exit(0)); }); ... setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 5_000).unref();
attest/apps/core/src/db.ts:942-943 — waitForConnections: true, connectionLimit: 10, (no queueLimit)
capacity_findings.quantification: Payments stranded per restart = arrival rate x pipeline duration (seconds in the sandbox, minutes on a real chain). A 10x T1 peak (10/s) for 60 s starts 600 concurrent chains; a T2 peak (1,000/s) starts tens of thousands, each making 4 partner calls with 20 s timeouts, so overload ends in mass EXCEPTION rather than queueing.
capacity_findings.fix: Durable jobs table (claimed with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) or a broker, with bounded worker concurrency and per-org fairness; a boot-time and periodic sweep of non-terminal payments; RFI timeout to CANCELLED; 429 when queue depth passes a limit.

capacity_findings.title: Webhook outbox ceiling: 20 per 2 s tick, sequential, 5 s timeout, i.e. 10 deliveries/s or about 0.9 payments/s
capacity_findings.affects: orgs that register a webhook_url; all orgs share one delivery loop
capacity_findings.claim: Delivery is one sequential loop per process: at most 20 rows per tick, one fetch at a time, a tick every 2 s (hardcoded), and it runs after promoteAnchored in the same tick. Each happy-path payment enqueues 11 webhooks, so orgs with a webhook URL saturate the outbox below 1 payment/s and the backlog grows without bound. A receiver that black-holes requests costs 5 s per attempt x 5 attempts = 25 s of the single loop per webhook, which starves every other org.

capacity_findings.quantification: Maximum 10 deliveries/s = 864k/day, about 78.5k payments/day at 11 webhooks each. T1 needs 11/s: the backlog grows about 86k/day and lag grows about 2.4 h per day. T2 needs 1,100/s (110x over); T3 needs 11,000/s. One org with a black-holed endpoint at only about 314 payments/day (275 s of loop time each) consumes the whole loop.
capacity_findings.fix: Concurrent delivery with per-endpoint concurrency caps and per-org queues; row claiming (a 'sending' status with a lease) for multiple instances; short connect timeout; a separate timer from promotion; coalescing of per-payment events.

capacity_findings.title: No compare-and-set on state and racy event sequencing: concurrent paths can lose updates or instruct a second transfer
capacity_findings.affects: cancel, rfi-response, BFI callbacks, multi-instance deployments
capacity_findings.claim: transition() reads the row, checks the order in JS, then UPDATEs by id only. appendEvent computes MAX(seq)+1 and then INSERTs, with no transaction. The only guard is UNIQUE (payment_id, seq), which makes one of two simultaneous appends fail at random. (a) Cancel vs approvalLeg: approvalLeg's UPDATE can land after cancel's and overwrite CANCELLED with PAYOUT_PRE_APPROVED, after which transferLeg instructs the wallet. The simulator refuses only because its BFI and wallet share one ledger record; a separate real settlement entity is never sent a cancel notice. (b) Two concurrent rfi-response calls both pass the checks and each schedules advance(), so two approval calls and two transfer calls can be made. (c) Duplicate or concurrent BFI callbacks re-run reconciliation and svc.issue.

capacity_findings.quantification: The race window is the SELECT-to-UPDATE gap in transition() plus the awaits before it. It widens as DB latency rises, so occurrences grow with load. The rail has no concurrency tests (test/remit.test.ts).
capacity_findings.fix: UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND state = ? with an affected-rows check, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in one transaction around event append and state change; atomic seq allocation; dedupe keys on rfi-response and on callbacks (partner event id); an idempotency key per payment_id on wallet instructions.

capacity_findings.title: Partner calls have no retry and no idempotency key; any failure is a terminal EXCEPTION
capacity_findings.affects: travel rule, payout approval, wallet transfer, settlement notice
capacity_findings.claim: Each payment makes four sequential partner calls in its critical path. post() does one fetch with a 20 s timeout and maps every network error or status of 400 or above to a 502. advance() turns any throw into a terminal EXCEPTION, and transition() refuses to leave a terminal state. A /wallet/transfer timeout is ambiguous, because the transfer may have happened, and there is no TXID lookup path, although design section 9 requires retrying only after a TXID lookup. No idempotency key is sent, so adding naive retries would risk double execution.

capacity_findings.title: Durable signed notifications, append-only signed event log, verified partner facts, idempotent SWIFT ids
capacity_findings.claim: Webhooks are written to a table before delivery, so they survive restarts; they are signed, retried with backoff, and backed by polling. Events are append-only with a unique (payment_id, seq), so a race fails loudly instead of corrupting the order. Every fact a partner asserts is signature-checked against the registry before it is stored. The payment id derived from the SWIFT UETR makes re-dropping a file safe.

capacity_findings.title: Partner integration sits behind interfaces
capacity_findings.claim: BfiConnector and SettlementWallet are the plug points, and TripleAProfileSim is just one implementation. Note that the interface as written expects transfer() to return a mined tx synchronously (see RR-06).

scale_path:
T1 (about 1/s sustained, 10/s peaks), in order: (1) Webhook outbox: concurrent delivery with per-endpoint caps, per-org fairness, its own timer separate from promotion, and claimed rows; otherwise the 10/s ceiling is below T1. (2) Recovery: a boot-time and periodic sweep that resumes non-terminal payments, plus an RFI timeout to CANCELLED. (3) Compare-and-set on state transitions (UPDATE ... WHERE state = ?) and atomic event seq, with dedupe on rfi-response and BFI callbacks. (4) Partner calls: idempotency key per (payment_id, leg), bounded retries into a non-terminal state, and a TXID lookup before any wallet re-instruction. (5) Event-driven or indexed promoteAnchored with a LIMIT. (6) Indexed exact-match SWIFT reference columns with server-side dedupe, replacing the SDK's LIKE searches. (7) Daily manifest as a root or in pages. (8) Exempt status polls from the synchronous audit write.

T2 (about 100/s, 1,000/s peaks): (1) Replace setImmediate with a durable job queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED or a broker) with bounded concurrency, per-org quotas and 429 backpressure. (2) Cut statements per payment from about 165: no read-after-write, no SELECT *, cached registry, subscription and KeyObjects, one transaction per leg, a larger pool or a dedicated remit pool, package_json in object storage. (3) Multi-instance readiness: platform key in an HSM or KMS, claimed or leader-elected worker rows, then scale core horizontally. (4) Move signing off the main thread (worker threads or HSM) and sign per leg rather than per event and per webhook. (5) Asynchronous settlement leg with a nonce manager or several hot wallets on a high-throughput L2, an explicit confirmation-depth finality rule, and real partner APIs (the simulator cannot sustain T1). (6) ETag, long-poll or push for bank status; a bulk submission endpoint for multi-transaction SWIFT files. (7) Retention and partitioning for webhook deliveries, quotes, idempotency keys and events; the registry snapshot referenced by hash.

T3 (about 1,000/s, 10,000/s peaks): (1) Net settlement: one on-chain transfer per corridor and BFI per interval, with a Merkle allocation per payment in the evidence, instead of one ERC-20 transfer per payment. (2) Bulk partner protocols (batched travel-rule messages, approvals and callbacks) and streaming notifications to banks instead of HTTP per event. (3) Shard the pipeline and MySQL by org or corridor, or move the event log to a stream with materialised state. (4) Batch signing (a signature over a Merkle root of events per interval) on signer clusters. (5) Capacity-plan MySQL commit throughput and the attest batcher (at least 1,000 leaves/s, i.e. one 1,024-leaf anchor per second).
open_questions: Query plans for anchoredPending, search(q=) and the console remit aggregates were not EXPLAINed, because the live MySQL on :3306 was off-limits. Confirm full scans on a copy.
There is no remit load test (deploy/seed-remit-volume.mjs defaults to 36 payments at concurrency 6). Per-payment CPU (about 10 ms) and latency are estimates; measure them with the simulator replaced.

Production partners do not exist in code (the Triple-A profile is simulated). We need the real BFI and settlement entity APIs: sync vs async, idempotency keys, callback retry semantics, bulk endpoints, rate limits.

No production settlement chain or custody stack is chosen, in code or in the design doc (which scopes everything as 'stage 0 sandbox'). L1 vs L2, confirmation depth, nonce management and HSM signing throughput decide whether T2 is feasible.
Is net settlement acceptable to the evidence model and to regulators? Today there is exactly one chainTransfer element per payment, with settlementIdMemo binding payment_id to tx.
How many institutions will the registry hold at T2/T3? This drives the RR-14 per-payment cost and the evidence package size.
Will banks rely on webhooks or on polling? That decides whether RR-02 or RR-08 bites first.

Attest reader: do evidence leaves from different orgs share one Merkle batch, and what anchor-confirmation latency applies on public Bitcoin? Together these set how long rows sit in BENEFICIARY_CREDIT_CONFIRMED and how large each promotion burst is.
Under a backlog, could payments fail the policy settlementWindow 'P2D' (evidence.ts:42) or the BFI approval validity (15 min in the simulator)? Not verified.
